clue.text: Inspect underground lab equipment

parts.note: to inspect something is to test it
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: Someone is told to check over the kit in a basement laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the everyday name for the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass tube closed at one end is a standard piece of chemistry apparatus.

clue.text: New parent? One could be boring

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for the tool itself

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of parent are made into something new

explanation.surface: A first-time parent wonders whether they will be dull company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' sounds like dull, but it means drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A trepan is a surgeon's cylindrical saw for cutting holes in the skull, a drilling tool.

clue.text: Fast run breaks Rod

indicators.note: breaks means splits open, so the run letter goes into the rod

parts.note: a stave is a stick or rod

explanation.surface: A quick run snaps a fishing rod.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run. 'Fast' looks like quick; it is going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to go without food, and to starve is to be deprived of food, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Taking just seconds for Steel, Nitro, Athena, Sabre and Giant

indicators.note: seconds here are the second letters, so only those are taken from each of the following words

parts.note: the second letters of these five words, one from each

explanation.surface: A list of TV Gladiators' names, all of them huge competitors, at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Steel, Nitro, Athena, Sabre and Giant were contestants on the British TV show Gladiators.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titans were a race of huge gods, so a titan is any colossus.

clue.text: Crook passing on 500 diamonds to be cut below

indicators.note: to be cut means removed, so both single letters come out of the combined words

parts.note: a crook in a path or arm is a bend
passing on is a euphemism for dying, so death
D is 500 in Roman numerals
D is the card-suit abbreviation

explanation.surface: A criminal dies and passes on a fortune in diamonds that must then be cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' is not a villain but a bend; 'passing on' is not handing over but dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneath is a preposition meaning lower than or under, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Leave centre of town to get wood

parts.note: to leave property to someone in your testament is to will it

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, here the two inside letters of town

parts.note: the two inside letters of town, leaving off its first and last

explanation.surface: Someone heads out of the middle of town to reach a stretch of woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like a departure, but it is the bequeathing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Willow is a timber, famously used to make cricket bats.

clue.text: A member of military popular with college class

definitions.note: a person description standing in for the phrase describing how such a person is dressed

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
uni is short for university
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A cadet is well liked among their college year.
explanation.definitionFit: A serving soldier is described as in uniform, the phrase also meaning enlisted in the forces.

clue.text: Occasionally recalling Eric Idle's first undergarments

indicators.note: first puts the idling word before the rest in the answer

parts.note: to idle is to linger, and the 's stands for is

indicators.note: recalling means calling back, so the selected letters are reversed
taking letters occasionally means only every other one of the word Eric

parts.note: the first and third letters of Eric, skipping the others

explanation.surface: Remembering Eric Idle of Monty Python and his first set of underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Idle the Python is split into two pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear and nightwear, so it is a collective term for undergarments.

clue.text: Wife scanned around the wound

indicators.note: around means the reading word goes round the other

parts.note: to scan a page is to read it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wife looks over the cut on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury, but it is the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreathed means twisted or coiled around, as smoke or a garland is wound about something.

clue.text: Turn in after 10 for example without being strict

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the example abbreviation wraps around the rest
after places the act-and-in piece behind the ten in the answer

parts.note: X is ten in Roman numerals
a turn is a performance, an act on stage
taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer is told to go on after the tenth act and not to be too demanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: An exacting person is demanding and severe, insisting on high standards, which is what strict means.

clue.text: Fruit compote less filling — one of five to start

indicators.note: to start puts the quintuplet piece at the front of the answer

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born together

indicators.note: the word compote without its filling keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters of compote, its middle gone

explanation.surface: Someone dishes out a stewed-fruit dessert with less in it, a fifth of the portion to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less filling' sounds like a lighter dessert, but it strips the middle from the word compote.
explanation.definitionFit: The quince is a hard, pear-shaped yellow fruit, usually cooked into jelly or paste.

clue.text: Look up and down?

parts.note: a glance, and in a down entry a word that reads the same upward as downward, a palindrome

explanation.surface: Someone is told to glance upward and then downward.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up and down' means read either way, and the four-letter word for a glance is the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A peep is a quick, furtive glance, and the word is a palindrome.

clue.text: Very adult books inside saw profit

indicators.note: inside puts the very-adult-books piece within the saying

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, an adage
NT is the New Testament, the usual crossword books

explanation.surface: A shop discovered that stocking explicit adult literature made money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is the noun for a proverb, not the past tense of see.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage is a benefit or gain, as in turning something to your advantage.

clue.text: Geek virtually infiltrating computer department still

indicators.note: infiltrating puts the shortened geek inside the department letters

parts.note: IT is information technology, the computer department

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the word is taken almost whole, losing its last letter

parts.note: a geek is a nerd

explanation.surface: A nerd more or less sneaks into the IT office unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like 'yet', but it is the adjective meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless and inactive, lacking the power to move, which is being still.

clue.text: Well-known drunk joining Cameo

parts.note: high means intoxicated
a cameo is a carved portrait in profile, and a short character sketch is also a profile

explanation.surface: A famous drunkard turns up in a brief cameo role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cameo' looks like a walk-on acting part; here it is the carved side-view portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone high-profile attracts a lot of public attention, so they are famous.

clue.text: Goal of pub stocking red wine I love

indicators.note: a pub stocking things keeps them inside, so the other letters go within

parts.note: an inn is a pub
tent is a dark red Spanish wine
taken as written
love is nil in tennis, the shape of O

explanation.surface: Someone states their aim: that the pub should stock the red wine they love.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is a deep red wine from Spain, mostly found in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: An intention is an aim or purpose, the thing you mean to achieve.

clue.text: See 14
Practise with drone armies regularly handle on site?

parts.note: to use a method is to practise it

indicators.note: regularly means at regular intervals, so every other letter of drone armies

parts.note: the second, fourth and every other letter after that of drone armies

explanation.surface: A military trainee drills with fleets of drones and controls them on location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' looks like a verb, but it is slang for a name, and a site is a website.
explanation.definitionFit: A username is the name you go by on a website, and handle is slang for a name.

clue.text: Heather carrying Jenny round as part of rodeo display

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the participle of what a cowboy does with a rope

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the heather word goes around the rest

parts.note: ling is a kind of heather
a jenny is a female donkey
a round thing is O-shaped

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather carries Jenny around during a rodeo show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' and 'Jenny' look like women's names; they are a plant and a female donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassoing is catching animals with a looped rope, a set piece of a rodeo.

clue.text: Race official in first place?

parts.note: the starter is the official who fires the gun to start a race
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A race official stands in pole position on the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First place' looks like a winning position; the question mark flags it as a first property bought.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter home is the small house or flat a first-time buyer purchases, their first place of their own.

clue.text: Zip line

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to move very fast
second meaning: a line of descent, a people or lineage

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a zip wire, but the words are two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash along at speed is to race, and a family or ethnic stock is also called a race.

clue.text: See 19
Keeping house, holding weapon extremely nervously

definitions.note: a noun, as in the phrase in keeping, meaning agreement

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the house letters go around the weapon

parts.note: an arm is a weapon

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of nervously

explanation.surface: Someone stays home, nervously clutching a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping' is a noun here, as in 'in keeping with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping is agreement or consistency, as in 'in keeping with', which is harmony.

clue.text: I note business is unstable

parts.note: taken as written
a firm is a business

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a company is shaky.
explanation.walkthrough: N is a note in the sense of a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm means weak and unsteady, physically frail, which is unstable.

clue.text: No heads rolled — perfect

indicators.note: rolled means turned over, so the combined words read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
tops are heads, the upper parts

explanation.surface: No heads fell from the guillotine, which went perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on means exactly right, completely accurate.

clue.text: Rinse out plastic component

indicators.note: out in the sense of wrong or disordered, so the letters of rinse are scrambled

explanation.surface: An instruction to rinse a plastic part clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Synthetic resins are the base material from which many plastics are made.

clue.text: Car put to work, assuming 6 is show time

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the other piece goes inside
put to work, the letters are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as part of the mix
taken as written as part of the mix
6 down is in uniform, written in the form IN U, since U is the radio-alphabet letter called Uniform

explanation.surface: A car is pressed into service as a theatre's opening approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: CAR and PUT rearranged give CURTAP, which takes in INU, the short form of 6 down IN UNIFORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtain up is the moment a theatre performance starts, when the curtain rises.

clue.text: Answer unlikely in any circumstances

parts.note: a tall story is an unlikely one

explanation.surface: An answer that is improbable whatever the situation.
explanation.definitionFit: At all is an emphatic phrase meaning in any way or whatever the conditions.

clue.text: Sharp police unit stopping spies from the East

indicators.note: stopping means plugging, so the police unit fills the gap in the spies
read from the east in an across answer is read right to left, so the spies come backwards

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued detective team interrupts eastern espionage.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic means sour-tasting and biting, and figuratively cutting, which is sharp.

clue.text: Singer from Tosca discovered Elvis rocks

indicators.note: rocks means shakes up, so the letters are mixed
dis-covered means with its covering removed, so the outer letters of Elvis go

parts.note: Elvis without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A singer from the opera Tosca finds out that Elvis is brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: Tosca is Puccini's opera; the music references are all decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalist is a singer, especially in a band or with an orchestra.

clue.text: Put some ginseng in everything as source of power

indicators.note: putting some of these words means taking a run of letters from inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of ginseng, the word in and the start of everything

explanation.surface: A health tip: add ginseng to every dish for an energy boost.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine is the machine that converts fuel into motion, the power plant of a vehicle.

clue.text: Plant drug in back of Tom Clancy novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: E is ecstasy

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of Tom
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hides narcotics at the back of a Tom Clancy thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book; it is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: The cyclamen is a flowering plant with upswept petals, popular as a winter houseplant.
